products.title: Coming Back to You: 2027 Visioning with Sarah Lakhani
products.body_html:
Welcome the new year with clarity, purpose, and inspiration!

Date & time: Sunday 15 November, 10am – 1pm

Back for the third year in a row, we are excited to welcome executive performance consultant Sarah Lakhani to the Mirzam Chocolate Factory for her 2027 planning workshop 'Coming Back to You'.

Coming Back to You: A Journey into 2027

A workshop to reflect on the past year and discover your true intentions for the year ahead.

This transformative workshop is your opportunity to pause, reflect on the year gone by, and align your intentions with what matters most in 2027. Through guided exercises and shared insights, you’ll reconnect with your true self, uncover what you truly desire, and focus on aligning your life with what matters most.

Whether you’re seeking personal growth, professional fulfillment, or both, this workshop will help you step into the new year with intention, alignment, and a sense of purpose that resonates deeply with who you are.

About Sarah Lakhani

I’m a brand and business consultant with 20+ years of experience advising leaders, founders, and organizations across Dubai and beyond. Through my boutique consulting firm, Sarah Lakhani Consulting, I help female executives and entrepreneurs align business and brand strategy so they can lead with clarity, build meaningful impact, and create work that reflects who they truly are.

Over the years, I’ve learned that strategy only works when the person behind it feels grounded, connected, and clear. That’s why, alongside my consulting work, I create spaces like this workshop that allow women to pause, reflect, release what has been heavy, and reconnect with themselves before stepping into a new chapter.

My approach blends structure, reflection and action, giving women the tools to return to themselves and move forward with calm confidence in life, in work, and in who they’re becoming.

products.title: Siniyah Salty Pearls - Small Tin
products.body_html:
This Salted Caramel Hazelnuts coated in 45% Milk Chocolate is more than just a delicious treat. It is a symbol of the pearling season, a time-honored tradition that dates back centuries in the United Arab Emirates.

‘Siniyah’ is the name of an island off Umm Al Quwain, where only a few years ago, the discovery of an ancient pearling town was announced.

Before the discovery of vast oil reserves in the 1930s, the way of life in the countries of the Persian Gulf differed significantly from the present one. The overwhelming majority of the male population of modern Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, and the adjacent territories was engaged in crafts directly related to the sea—they were fishermen, shipbuilders, sailors, and pearl divers.

The latter industry, already quite exotic if measured against today’s standards, was then the most profitable—especially for ship captains and merchants who resold pearls to other countries.

Pearling was once the lifeblood of the country, providing sustenance and employment for a significant portion of the population.

Although the pearling industry collapsed by the early 1900s, the memories and traces of this historical golden period are still ingrained in the hearts of the people of the UAE.

products.title: Siniyah Salty Pearls - Big Tin
products.body_html:
This Salted Caramel Hazelnuts coated in 45% Milk Chocolate is more than just a delicious treat. It is a symbol of the pearling season, a time-honored tradition that dates back centuries in the United Arab Emirates.

‘Siniyah’ is the name of an island off Umm Al Quwain,
where only a few years ago, the discovery of an
ancient pearling town was announced.

Before the discovery of vast oil reserves in the 1930s, the
way of life in the countries of the Persian Gulf differed
significantly from the present one. The overwhelming
majority of the male population of modern Bahrain,
Qatar, Kuwait, and the adjacent territories was
engaged in crafts directly related to the sea—they were
fishermen, shipbuilders, sailors, and pearl divers.
The latter industry, already quite exotic if measured
against today’s standards, was then the most
profitable—especially for ship captains and merchants who resold pearls to other countries.

Pearling was once the lifeblood of the country, providing sustenance and employment for a significant portion of the population.

Although the pearling industry collapsed by the early 1900s, the memories and traces of this historical golden period are still ingrained in the hearts of the people of the UAE.

products.title: Sinyah Salty Pearls - Caramelised Hazelnuts in 45% Salted Milk Chocolate
products.body_html:
This Salted Caramel Hazelnuts coated in 45% Milk Chocolate is more than just a delicious treat. It is a symbol of the pearling season, a time-honored tradition that dates back centuries in the United Arab Emirates.

‘Siniyah’ is the name of an island off Umm Al Quwain,
where only a few years ago, the discovery of an
ancient pearling town was announced.

Before the discovery of vast oil reserves in the 1930s, the
way of life in the countries of the Persian Gulf differed
significantly from the present one. The overwhelming
majority of the male population of modern Bahrain,
Qatar, Kuwait, and the adjacent territories was
engaged in crafts directly related to the sea—they were
fishermen, shipbuilders, sailors, and pearl divers.
The latter industry, already quite exotic if measured
against today’s standards, was then the most
profitable—especially for ship captains and merchants who resold pearls to other countries.

Pearling was once the lifeblood of the country, providing sustenance and employment for a significant portion of the population.

Although the pearling industry collapsed by the early 1900s, the memories and traces of this historical golden period are still ingrained in the hearts of the people of the UAE.

For thousands of years, people have relied on the coconut tree for wood, fiber, and fruit. Early Arabian spice traders sailed the Monsoon winds to India in dhows built from coconut wood and tied together with coconut rope.

As far back as 2,000 years ago, coconuts were being carried from India to East Africa, earning the name "zhawzhat al-hind", meaning “walnut of India,” a term still found in Arabic dialects today.

products.title: 72% Dark Chocolate Single Origin Papua New Guinea
products.body_html:
This bar carries bold, smoky flavor notes developed during the drying process. After fermentation, the cacao beans are spread on raised trays above smoldering coals. As the smoke rises, it gently infuses the beans—flavoring the cocoa butter itself. The result is a rich, intense chocolate with a distinct smoky finish you can taste in every bite.

All of our single origin plantation choices have been led by the history and stories of the maritime Spice Route, and countries who traded with fragrant and exotic goods hundreds of years ago.

products.title: 62% Dark Chocolate with Cardamom & Coffee
products.body_html:
Across the Middle East, families create and grind their signature coffee blends, served to guests with a blend of spices, ‘Gahwa’.

Taking our cue from this tradition, and the strong coffee trading history from this region (Mocha in Yemen was for a long time the worlds busiest port for coffee) we have created this delicious recipe.

This bar is made with 62% single origin dark chocolate infused with cardamom and freshly roasted coffee (from a local Dubai roaster around the corner).

products.body_html: A gently spiced bar that brings together two iconic spices of the ancient Spice Route—warm cinnamon and aromatic star anise—layered with tender slices of organic dried figs from Turkey. All are folded into smooth 62% single origin dark chocolate, creating a bar that is rich, fragrant, and softly sweet, with a luxurious texture and a hint of nostalgia in every bite.
